notes: The test plots the terrain's look is perfected on (roadmap L1, docs/scenery/TERRAIN_ROADMAP.md part A; the catalogue in docs/research/TERRAIN_PROCEDURAL_METHOD_2026-11.md section 6.2). Each is found on the map by its anchor, as the views are (data/scenery/views.json), and seen from three cameras looking at its middle: eye (1.7 m, 30 m back), low (25 m, 43 m back) and high (150 m, 260 m back) (simcore/scenery/plots.hpp). A field_layer anchor finds the nearest field within 3 km of close_km whose whole 50 m square is one parcel in that ground layer on the scenario's day (with edge set true, the cameras look at where that field ends toward them, from outside it: a standing crop's face); turn_deg turns the cameras from the anchor's own bearing (a field's: its furrows). Close to battery 21's district (10 m ground) where it can be. Photos are ids in views.json's register. Rendered by -SimMapShots=<folder> -SimShotSet=plots, set beside their photographs and their last approved render by tools/plot_lab.py. Presentation only.

plots.name: Ploughland (autumn)
plots.must_see: Furrows along the parcel's heading at the plough's 30-50 cm, big dry clods, a pale dusty top; the headland worked across the furrows; the parcel's edge against its neighbour.

plots.name: Maize stover (harvested)
plots.must_see: Stalks lying and broken, stumps in rows 70-76 cm apart, cut stalks or bales in places.

plots.name: Standing maize (dry)
plots.must_see: A 2-3 m wall of dry tan stalks in rows; the field's edge as a face.

plots.name: Wheat stubble
plots.must_see: Short straw 10-20 cm in the drill's rows, the combine's straw lines, weeds.

plots.name: Forest edge against a field
plots.must_see: The herb fringe, a shrub belt, a mantle of lower trees, then the stand; never a wall.

plots.name: Road with verge and ditch
plots.must_see: Asphalt 4-6 m, earth shoulders 1-2 m, a ditch, a pole line, a tree row on one side.

plots.name: River bank with reeds
plots.must_see: A reed belt 1-5 m wide, reeds 2-4 m tall, willows on the bank.
